summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored Irish documents (Dáil records 1994-2005 on the investment-based naturalisation scheme, the 2004 Act, IIP launch, guidelines 2012-2019, web pages, closure press release, the 2017 internal evaluation and the two EY reviews of 2020). 162 new observations, 8 events, 1 term, 5 proposed indicators. ledger.contains: Dáil oral answers (13 questions taken together) on investment-linked naturalisation, 25 Oct 1994: Government-approved terms of reference for the advisory group (IR£1m net per applicant, residence kept 5 years, 60 days in 2 years, 7-year loans, Forfás monitoring); Government decision to legislate; Attorney General advice on 29 applications approved in principle; approvals 1992-94 (39, corrected 1992 figure 20, 25 low-interest loans, 2 loans plus shares, 3 forestry); 7 granted in 1994 to June; 1 approved since 1 June 1994; 22 received in 1994; former working rule of about IR£500,000. Supplementary questions from deputies (no new figures). One approved case is described (IR£1m investment in a Co. Limerick company, about 100 jobs saved and 82 to be created): single-case figures kept in notes, not as programme rows. Rows already in the data (20, 39, 25, 29, 22, terms, ToR event) were not duplicated.

Whole day's Dáil record of 14 June 1994 (oral and written answers on many subjects). In scope: written answer to Qs 66, 74, 75 on investment-linked naturalisation (granted: 17 in 1992, 15 in 1993, 7 in 1994 to date; nationalities listed without counts: USA, Uruguay, Kuwait, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Hong Kong, Canada, Philippines, Netherlands; pre-1992 data not available), all three already in the data; answers to Qs 69 and 73 (no figures); Taoiseach's oral questions on the C & D Foods controversy (no programme statistics; a deputy's 'over £500,000' about one investment, not recorded). Out of scope: written answer to Q76 with general naturalisation applications, certificates and refusals 1989-1993 (all naturalisation, not investment-linked), and the rest of the day's business. Note the 1992 figure (17) was corrected to 20 on 25 Oct 1994 (irl-dail-pq-1994-10-25).

Dáil priority question of 25 June 1998 on the passports-for-investment scheme, with the Minister's summary of the Department's review (10 Feb 1998) and Appendices A-F placed in the Official Report: history and Government decisions 1989-1997; naturalisations 1988-94 (66 investors + 39 family) and since 1994 (29 + 9), total 143 persons (48 family); 19 committed and 50 deferred cases at 4 Sep 1996; 5 older uncompleted approvals and 8 dependants' applications on hand at 10 Feb 1998; Appendix A Statement of Intent (60 days, residence); Appendix B compliance table for the 66 early cases (6 conditions, yes/no); Appendix C 1994 terms of reference (IR£1m); Appendix D compliance table for the 29 later cases; Appendix E investment by sector (IR£90m total); Appendix F press release of 20 Apr 1998 ending the scheme; list of countries said to sell citizenship (no numbers); debate: 40 certificates issued by Minister Owen, 4 granted by the 1994-97 Government after the cut-off, a deputy's '11 passports' to Saudi and Pakistani nationals; jobs 'in the thousands' (words, not recorded); a deputy's hypothetical about borrowing at 3% and investing at 11% (not recorded). Appendix E sectors sum to 90 as printed. Earlier rows (66, 39, 29, 9, 143, 48, IR£90m and 14 sectors, terms, 4 events) not duplicated. Appendix D 'No' dashes not recorded as zeros. Two new indicators proposed for the compliance tables.

Dáil priority question of 17 Oct 2002: publication of the review group report (4 Aug 2002); the Minister's view of the scheme (introduced 1988, suggested 1986, changed in 1994, no statutory basis); his examination of the file on 11 passports and naturalisations found 'irregular and unusual'; all pre-1997 files sought by the Moriarty tribunal; history of the 1994 internal inquiry; the Minister's pledge never to recommend selling citizenship again. Only number about the programme: the 11 naturalisations (recorded). Existing event on the 11 passports not duplicated.

Written answer of 22 Nov 2005 (Q512): 107 primary investors and 76 spouses and minor children naturalised 1989-2004 (both already in the data); confidentiality policy; scheme abolished April 1998 and ruled out by the 2004 Act (event already in the data). Nothing else in scope.

Written answer of 14 Dec 2004 (Q299): the 1995 internal report and 2002 findings; the 2002 review group report says over £100 million was invested (in the data); files on 128 persons with the Moriarty tribunal (added, new indicator proposed); 107 primary investors plus 76 spouses and minor children, 183 citizens (in the data; 107 + 76 = 183); no records of passports kept; Government approval to abolish the scheme and the 2004 Act provision.

Dáil second-stage debate on the Irish Nationality and Citizenship Bill 2004, 27 Oct 2004. Mostly about citizenship of children born in Ireland to non-national parents (out of scope). In scope: the Minister's statement that section 10 (narrow definition of 'Irish associations') ends investment-based naturalisation (event already in the data), the October 2003 Government support for Senator Quinn's bill (event added), deputies' remarks on the scheme (no post mortem, Moriarty tribunal, revocation, named investors) including the claim of 11 passports issued in one day (added as claim). Other numbers (e.g. 1.8 million Irish passport holders born abroad) are out of scope.

Dáil debate on the Irish Nationality and Citizenship Bill 1999, 13 Apr 2000: mainly post-nuptial citizenship, birth on the island of Ireland and residence rules (out of scope). On the investment scheme, only words: a deputy's view that bona fide investments created lasting jobs, and the Minister's statement that the Government abolished the scheme on 20 April 1998 (event already in the data from irl-dail-pq-1998-06-25) 'which had commenced in 1989', that he set up a review group on investment-based naturalisation (Departments, Enterprise Ireland, IDA and two outside experts; report expected, not dated) and that remaining pipeline cases were still being processed. No programme numbers and no new dated event.

Text of the Irish Nationality and Citizenship Act 2004 (16 sections: citizenship by birth for children of non-nationals, reckonable residence, naturalisation conditions, offences with fines up to €3,000/€50,000). The Act does not mention investment; section 10 (inserting s.16(2) into the 1956 Act) defines 'Irish associations' as blood, affinity or adoption, which removed the basis of the investment scheme. That change is already an event (2004-12-15, sourced to the Dáil debate irl-dail-debate-2004-10-27). No programme numbers or terms; commencement by ministerial order (date not in the text).

INIS statement (March 2012) formally launching the Immigrant Investor Programme and the Start-up Entrepreneur Programme: open from 15 April 2012 (launch event already in the data); IIP options (endowment €500,000; enterprise €1,000,000 for 3 years; €2,000,000 five-year NTMA bond, single 5.1% payment = 1% AER; mixed €1,000,000 = €500k property + €500k bonds); 2+3 year residence permission then 5-year renewals; visit once in 12 months; no naturalisation concession (5 years' residence); Evaluation Committee membership; €750 application fee. All these terms are already in program_terms from the 2012 guidelines (same values), so no duplicate term rows were added. Start-up Entrepreneur Programme (€75k funding) is a separate entrepreneur scheme, out of scope. No statistics.

INIS 'Investor and Entrepreneur Schemes' web page captured Nov 2016: notice that no applications would be accepted for the next evaluation meeting until 2 January 2017 because of rising applications; next closing date 14 Sep 2016; bond (€1m) and mixed (€950k) options suspended from 18 July 2016 (both events already in the data); table of options then in force (bond €1m at 0%, enterprise €500,000 for 3 years, approved funds €500,000, REIT €2m, mixed €450k property + €500k bond, endowment €500,000 or €400,000 pooled by 5+), 2+3 year permission then 5-year tranches, visit once a year. All terms already in program_terms (from irl-inis-changes-pr-2013 and the 2014 guidelines, same values). No statistics.

Department of Justice press release of 14 Feb 2023 closing the IIP to applications from close of business 15 Feb 2023 (closure event in the data): approved investment of almost €1.252 billion since inception and approximately 1,500 cases on hand (both in the data); summary of conditions at closure (net worth €2m; enterprise €1m, approved fund €1m, REIT €2m, endowment €500,000 or €400,000 pooled; bond and mixed options suspended in 2016; all already in program_terms); existing projects continue and may source new investors; three months for well-developed projects and under-subscribed approved funds to submit applications (described in words in the closure event context; no new numbers). STEP continues (out of scope).

IIP Guidelines 2012 (18 pp.): purpose; why invest in Ireland (general tax facts, out of scope); four options (bond €2,000,000 5-year 1%; enterprise €1,000,000 for 3 years incl. VC-fund rule with worked example; mixed €1,000,000 max 50% property, or property ≥€1,000,000 of clear benefit; endowment €500,000); application process and documents; 2-year permission, 3-year renewal, then 5-year renewals; family members; naturalisation in the normal way; €750 non-refundable fee. All option amounts and the fee are already in program_terms from this document. No statistics.

IIP 2014 Guidelines (31 pp., enhanced July 2013 terms): net worth €2m; bond €1m at 0%; enterprise €500,000 for 3 years; approved fund €500,000; REIT €2m (new) with retention rules (hold 3 years, then divest at most 50%, a further 25% after 4 years, free after 5); mixed €450,000 property + €500,000 bond; endowment €500,000 or €400,000 pooled by 5+; €750 fee; education-expense discount up to €50,000 (term added); FAQ: committee meets every three months, applications take on average three to four months (added), 1 day a year in Ireland, enterprises must have 60% of staff and costs in Ireland; local property tax rates (general tax, out of scope). REIT divestment schedule is described here for the REIT term note (not a separate amount).

IIP Guidelines December 2016, amended August 2017 (29 pp.): six options with bond (€1.0m, 0%) and mixed (€450,000 + €500,000) marked 'currently suspended'; enterprise €1.0m and approved fund €1.0m for 3 years (from 2 Jan 2017); REIT €2m and retention rules; endowment €500,000 / €400,000 pooled; fee €1,500; net worth €2m; education discount up to €50,000; FAQ: committee meets 4-5 times a year, three to four months average (added), 1 day a year; submission by email (Aug 2017 amendment, procedural). Option amounts and fee already in program_terms (fund and fee from this document; enterprise from irl-oir-wa-2017-11-16). No statistics.

IIP Guidelines January 2018 (34 pp., submission rules amended December 2017): same terms as December 2016 (net worth €2m; enterprise and fund €1.0m; REIT €2m with retention; endowment €500,000 / €400,000; fee €1,500; education discount up to €50,000; bond and mixed no longer listed), process, documents for approval and renewal, family; FAQ: committee meets 4-5 times a year, applications take on average 16 to 18 weeks (added, new indicator processing_time_weeks proposed), 1 day per calendar year. All amounts already in program_terms. No statistics.

IIP Guidelines for Applicants, February 2019 (19 pp.): same thresholds (net worth €2m; enterprise €1m, approved fund €1m, REIT €2m for 3 years with retention schedule; endowment €500,000 / €400,000 pooled; fee €1,500 by EFT); process: investment within 90 days of the pre-approval letter, solicitor's confirmation of €2m net worth, permission 2 years, then 3, then 5 (write 3 months ahead); education discount up to €50,000; anti-money-laundering obligations (2018 Act); FAQ: three to four months average (added), 1 day per calendar year. All amounts already in program_terms. No statistics.

Department of Justice (IGEES) interim evaluation of the IIP, data to end-March 2017 (48 pp.). Contains: applications by application year 2012-Q1 2017 and amounts in submitted and approved applications (Table 3.1-3.2; approved column and option totals were already in the data; submitted column, totals and 2017 projections added); place of residence of applicants (Table 3.3, added); option shares of applications and approvals (Table 3.4, added); family make-up of applicants (Table 3.5, added); ~260 approvals, ~512 dependants and ~770 permits in 2016 (added); staff costs €0.40m and fees €0.29m 2012-16 (added); ~50 enterprise investments (added); enterprise investment and construction jobs by year (Table 6.2, added), approved applicants, projects and sustained jobs by sector (Table 6.4, added), gross/net benefit and employment (Tables 6.6-6.7, added; new indicator rbi_economic_benefit_estimate proposed); option terms (Table 1.1; already in program_terms); recommendations; agent survey; evaluation-committee facts (12 members, 4-5 meetings a year).
